retained_primary_inputs.title: Quantitative properties of the non-properness set of a polynomial map
retained_primary_inputs.role: Explicit proof input: Definition 2.1, Proposition 2.2, Definition 2.3, and Theorem 3.2. For a generically finite polynomial map from complex affine space, its nonproperness set is covered by nonconstant polynomial images of A1. Only this qualitative conclusion is used, not the degree bound.

retained_primary_inputs.title: On closed rational functions in several variables
retained_primary_inputs.portions_inspected: Section 2, Lemmas 1 and 2 and their proofs; Definition 1; Lemma 2(1) equivalence of closedness and noncomposition.
retained_primary_inputs.role: Explicit proof input: Lemma 2(1), equivalence (a)--(c), a noncomposite rational function over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field generates a relatively algebraically closed subfield. The reduced-pencil ramification proof and the one-exception polynomial test are written directly in the new note.
Proof input: characteristic-zero Riemann-Hurwitz, Section 53.12 and Lemmas 53.12.2/4. The finite-affine-line constant-field descent consequence is proved in the note.

Explicit proof input: Lemma 15.113.3 multiplicativity of ramification indices, Definition 15.113.7 and the finite-etale criterion in the proof of Lemma 15.113.8. Only finite extensions of characteristic-zero divisorial DVRs are used.

Section 58.13, inertia definition, Lemmas 58.13.1-2, Example 58.13.3 and Lemma 58.13.4: inertia kernels describe the unramified quotient; for a regular base codimension-one inertia suffices by purity.

Lemma 58.21.4: a quasi-finite normal cover of a regular base, unramified in codimension one, is etale. Applied only to a finite normal quotient cover over complex affine space. Here also applied on the regular open torus after killing all non-axis divisorial inertia.

Retained version 2.21, printed page 28, paragraph before Theorem 3.4: finite etale complex covers give finite topological coverings. Only this forward direction is used; contractibility of C^n then excludes a connected cover of degree greater than one. Here the forward comparison on (C*)^2 makes a connected finite Galois group a quotient of Z^2, hence abelian.
